Here is a comprehensive, trainer-ready 12‑week plan summary for your client. It integrates:
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Hypertrophy Foundation
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Push-intensity emphasis, higher push load, power/power day, HIIT, and cardio framework
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Max strength and peak hypertrophy, with a plyometric/power day kept in
- Cardio plan (SSC, LMI, optional HIIT)
- Plyometric/Power day
- Hypertrophy nutrition plan (calorie/macro targets, peri-workout fueling)
- 1RM test at end of Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) with progression plan

Starting details assumed
- Client: 26-year-old female, recreational lifter
- Frequency: 4 lifting days/week, plus cardio (2–3 days) and optional HIIT
- Start: 2026-06-01
- Equipment: barbell/dumbbells available; optional machines/boxes for plyometrics

1) Weekly structure (4 lifting days + cardio + optional HIIT and plyometric day)
- Monday: Upper Push (Phase 2 push-intensity emphasis in Weeks 5–8)
- Tuesday: Lower Day (Strength focus early; transition to hypertrophy/accessory as needed)
- Wednesday: Cardio (SSC/LMI) + optional HIIT or rest
- Thursday: Upper Pull
- Friday: Plyometric/Power Day (Weeks 1–4 introduced lightly; Weeks 5–8 integrated with power focus; Weeks 9–12 maintain with technique)
- Saturday: Lower Day (Hypertrophy/Accessory emphasis in Phase 1; Phase 2/3 balance)
- Sunday: Rest

2) Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 – Hypertrophy Foundation
Goal: Build muscle mass, establish movement patterns, prepare CNS for heavier loads.
- Week 1 (Hypertrophy Foundation)
  - Day 1 Upper Push: Bench 4x8–10; Overhead Press 3x10–12; Incline DB 3x10–12; Lateral Raises 3x12–15; Triceps Pushdowns 3x12–15
  - Day 2 Lower Hypertrophy: Back Squat 4x8–10; RDL 3x8–10; Leg Press 3x12–15; Leg Curls 3x12–15; Calf Raises 4x15–20
  - Day 3 Rest/Light cardio
  - Day 4 Upper Pull: Barbell/Dumbbell Row 4x8–10; Lat Pulldown 3x10–12; Seated Row 3x10–12; Face Pulls 3x12–15; Curls 3x12–15
  - Day 5 Lower Hypertrophy/Accessory: Front Squat/Goblet 3x10–12; Hip Thrust/Glute Bridge 3x10–12; Bulgarian Split Squat 3x10–12 per leg; Abs 3x45–60s/ Pallof 3x12–15
  - Optional cardio/core day
- Week 2: Hypertrophy Emphasis
  - Similar structure with slight increases in volume/weight
- Week 3: Progressive Overload
  - Increase loads as form allows; consider adding a set to compounds
- Week 4: Deload Prep
  - Reduce volume ~40–50%; maintain technique; mobility focus

3) Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 – Push-intensity emphasis, higher pushing load
Key changes
- Push primary emphasis: Bench and Overhead Press at higher intensities
- Accessory push work limited to quality volume to balance pulling
- Maintain lower body work and pulling work to balance fatigue
- Introduce dedicated Plyometric/Power Day (Weeks 5–8)
- Cardio: SSC/LMI remains; HIIT introduced as an optional day every other week
- Week 5
  - Day 1 Upper Push-Heavy: Bench 5x5; Overhead Press 4x5–6; Barbell Row 4x6–8; Incline DB 3x8–10; Lateral Raises 3x12–15; Triceps Pushdowns 3x10–12
  - Day 2 Lower Strength: Squat 5x5; RDL 4x6–8; Leg Press 3x8–10; Core Pallof 3x12
  - Day 4 Upper Pull: Row variations 4x6–8; Lat Pulldown 3x8–10; Seated Row 3x8–10; Face Pulls 3x12–15; Curls 3x10–12
  - Day 5 Lower Hypertrophy/Accessory: Front Squat/Goblet 3x8–10; Hip Thrust 3x8–12; Split Squat 3x8–10/leg; Abs 3x12–15
- Week 6
  - Similar structure with progression on main push lifts (e.g., 5x4 on bench; 4x5 on OHP)
  - Accessory adjustments to preserve pulling balance
- Week 7
  - Push Intensity Peak: Bench 5x3–4; OHP 4x4–5; Barbell Rows 4x6; Incline DB 3x8–10; Accessory as above; push/pull balance
  - Lower: Squat 5x3–4; RDL 4x6; Leg Curl 3x8–12
  - Upper Pull + Push Superset Focus day
- Week 8: Deload / Technique Day
  - 40–50% volume; main lifts 2–3 sets x 3–5 reps at lighter loads
  - Plyometric Day scales back; maintain technique
  - Optional light testing if client ready

4) Phase 2: Plyometric/Power Day (weekly, integrated)
- Purpose: develop explosive power and rate of force development
- Structure (rough 45–60 min):
  - Warm-up: 10 minutes (dynamic mobility, light plyometrics)
  - Power block (lower body focus; 3–4 exercises): loaded jump squats/box jumps 3x3–5; broad jumps 3x3–4; tempo single-leg box step-down into jump 3x6 per leg; med ball slam or push-press 3x6–8
  - Post-activation or plyo finisher: 2 sets of light jump variations or pogo hops
  - Core/anti-rotation 5–10 min
  - Cool-down: mobility
- Safety: emphasize form; low volume and proper landing mechanics; avoid when joints are fatigued from prior sessions

5) Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 – Max Strength and Peak Hypertrophy
Goal: Peak strength, maintain hypertrophy, refine technique
- Week 9 (Max Strength Push Day): Upper Body heavy with 5x3 on bench; 4x4 on OHP; Row 4x4–6; Accessory as needed
- Week 10: Maintain heavy lifts with 4–5x3–5 on major lifts; accessory work lighter
- Week 11: Volume taper with near-max reps
- Week 12: Taper to finishing week; optional 1RM attempts if client is ready
- Testing window: End of Week 12 or following rest week

6) 1RM Test at end of Phase 3
- Lifts: Squat, Bench, Deadlift (optional Overhead Press)
- Testing plan: Two-day approach preferred to reduce fatigue
  - Day A: Squat + Bench (warm-up ladder; attempts sequence)
  - Day B: Deadlift + Overhead Press (warm-up ladder; attempts sequence)
- Warm-up: 5–10 minutes cardio; mobility; ramp up 40–60% x5–8; 60–70% x3–5; 75–85% x2–3; 90%+ single rep
- Attempt progression: Start conservative; if first attempt solid, proceed to second; allow adequate rest
- 1RM calculation: If using 3–5RM, convert to 1RM with Epley (1RM = weight × (1 + reps/30))
- Data capture: 1RM value, RPE of final attempt, notes on technique, fatigue
- If testing is too fatiguing, use 3RM/5RM testing and calculate estimated 1RM
- Using results: set new loading targets for Phase 4; adjust progression rates; recalibrate nutrition if needed

7) Cardio plan (integrated)
- SSC (Steady-State) 2 days/week; 25–45 minutes depending on phase
- LMI (Low-to-Moderate Intensity Intervals) 1 day/week; intervals 30 seconds on with 60–90 seconds rest
- HIIT: Optional day every 2 weeks; 6–8 rounds of 20–30 seconds near max with 2–3 minutes rest
- Plyometric day: 1 weekly, integrated as described
- Scheduling: prefer non-lifting days or after lifting with minimal impact on heavy days

8) Nutrition for hypertrophy (summary)
- Daily calories: +250–500 kcal/day above maintenance; start around +300 kcal
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg (target 1.8–2.0 g/kg)
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg (start ~3.5–4.5 g/kg)
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg
- Peri-workout: Pre 20–40 g carbs + 10–20 g protein; Post 0.25–0.4 g/kg protein + 0.5 g/kg carbs
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day baseline
- Supplements: protein powder, creatine 3–5 g/day, vitamin D, omega-3 if needed
- Tracking: weekly weigh-ins; 1–2 week macro adjustments as needed
- On COC: no cycle adjustments required; fatigue management if needed by adjusting volume

9) Progress tracking and progression rules
- Use a training log (sets x reps x load) with RPE
- Aim for gradual increases in load when all reps completed with good form
- If a session is suboptimal, back off load 5–10% and rebuild
- Reassess 1RM at end of Phase 3 to set new baselines

10) Safety and modifications
- Spotters for heavy bench/squat as needed
- Warm-ups prioritized; technique over load
- If pain arises, substitute with safer alternatives and notify the client

11) Deliverables and how I can customize
- Ready-to-print 12-week calendar with week-by-week sessions (exercises, sets, reps, loads, RPE targets)
- Precise Phase 2 Weeks 5–8 push-intensity block rewritten with exact sets/reps and progression rules
- Phase 3 Week 9–12 plan, including plyometric/power day, HIIT, and cardio integration
- Full 1RM test protocol (two-day option) with ladder, warm-up, and data sheet
- Nutrition plan aligned to this structure with weekly targets and sample menus
- Optional substitutions based on available equipment

Overall approach

Preparation protocol (2–3 weeks lead-in)

- Maintain technique focus and warm-up routines; avoid testing fatigue from prior heavy sessions.
- Ensure 1–2 rest days before the test day to optimize performance.

Testing order (recommended)
- Do not test all lifts in a single day if fatigue is a concern. If you must, sequence from least to most fatiguing and allow extra warm-up. A safer approach is to test across two days:
  - Day A: Squat and Bench Press
  - Day B: Deadlift and Overhead Press (optional 1RM)

Warm-up protocol for each lift
- General warm-up: 5–10 minutes light cardio and dynamic mobility (hips, thoracic, ankles, shoulders).
- Specific warm-up progression for each lift:
  - 1–2 sets with 40–60% of anticipated 1RM for 5–8 reps
  - 1–2 sets with 60–70% for 3–5 reps
  - 1 set with 75–85% for 2–3 reps
  - 1 set with 90%+ for 1 rep (as a confidence booster)
- Rest intervals: 2–3 minutes between heavier attempts; longer rests (3–5 minutes) for squats and deadlifts if needed.

Prediction/estimation method (if not testing all lifts)
- If you test a 3RM or 5RM, estimate 1RM using Epley:
  - 1RM = Weight × (1 + Reps/30)
  - Example: 5 reps with 100 kg => 1RM ≈ 100 × (1 + 5/30) = 116.7 kg
- If you test 4–6 RM, you can use alternative formulas (Brzycki is common: 1RM = W × (36/(37−R))). For simplicity, many coaches rely on 3–5RM testing and convert to 1RM.

- Squat: target 5–15 kg gain in 12 weeks, with proportional increases if technique, mobility, and trunk stability are solid.
- Deadlift: target 5–15 kg gain; expect slightly higher variability due to technique and ROM.
- Overhead Press (optional): target 3–6 kg gain; smaller gains are common due to shoulder stability demand.

Safety and readiness criteria
- No pain in joints, no unusual dizziness, no acute injury.
- Movement quality: maintain strict form; no grinding or butt-wouncing on squats; bar speed remains controlled.
- If form degrades or pain arises, stop and switch to a submaximal estimate using a 3RM/5RM trial or postpone the test.
